note: Tecmo Super Bowl (NES) rates the 1990 NFL season. Every player of its 28 clubs but the punters as [name, franchise (scripts/data/nfl-teams.json), Tecmo slot, game position, overall, { rom: the game's spelling, no: jersey, attributes, id: nflverse gsis id }], written by scripts/sync-tecmo.mjs. The overall is ours, not the game's (conversion).

dump.about: TSBTool Supreme's data file of the stock NES cartridge (28 clubs, 30 players each).

checks.name: Tecmo Geek
checks.about: Tecmo Geek's list of every NES player: the attributes it shows (those that differ between players and that the game uses), its position labels and its ratings.
differences: John Taylor (49ers WR1): REC 69 in the dump, 63 at Tecmo Geek

names.about: A player takes nflverse's name when he is on his club's nflverse roster that season (or the one before or after) under the game's name: last names equal, cut short or a letter apart (two in a long name), first names equal, his given name, an initial, a short form or a letter or two apart, never both approximate. Else the game's spelling in ordinary capitals (gameSpelling). nflverse has no gsis id for some of the players it names.

notes: John Taylor (San Francisco, WR1) has receptions 69 in the dump and 63 at Tecmo Geek. Nothing settles which the cartridge holds; the dump's 69 is kept.

NES Tecmo Super Bowl has only eleven defenders a club, two of them corners, and three linemen in its 3-4: the game's nickel lineup is a corner and a lineman short, and fills them out of position. No player is added.

conversion.overall: Ours, not the game's: Tecmo rates no overall. Each player's Tecmo Geek score at his game position is ranked among the season's players at that position (mid-rank percentile, ties sharing one) and read off Madden NFL 2002's overalls at that position (the 2001 season: maddenratings.net's 31 team spreadsheets, punters left out), as many of each Madden team's best as the season carries per club, by linear interpolation; rounded and held to 1–99.

formula.about: Tecmo Geek's player ratings (https://www.tecmogeek.com/about/ratings/): per position, each attribute scored against the best value at the position (hitting power by bands), weighted to 100. Backs are rated as rushers, receivers and tight ends as receivers.

conversion.attributes: By the game's screen names, on its 16-step scale (6, 13 ... 100): RS running speed, RP rushing power, MS maximum speed, HP hitting power, BB body balance, AG agility, PS passing speed, PC pass control, PA passing accuracy, AR avoid rush (Tecmo Geek: avoid pass block), CO coolness, BC ball control, REC receptions, PI pass interceptions, QU quickness, KP kicking power, KA kicking ability, AKB avoid kick block.

positions.slots: QB QB; RB RB; WR WR; TE TE; C, LG, RG, LT, RT OL; RE, NT, LE DL; ROLB, RILB, LILB, LOLB LB; RCB, LCB CB; FS, SS S; K K; P left out.
positions.skill: Backs, receivers and tight ends play the position Tecmo Geek labels them with. It reads the one-back clubs' second back's slot as a receiver's and their third receiver's as a back's (Phoenix and Washington), and the run-and-shoot clubs' tight ends' slots as receivers' too (Atlanta, Detroit and Houston: six receivers, four backs, no tight end).
positions.defence: Defenders play their slot's position, as the game has them (a tackle at inside linebacker is a linebacker).
